source.title: Hippocampal neurons construct a map of an abstract value space

confidence_rationale: High-quality primate single-unit recording (Cell 2021) and MECH-144's second founding citation. It is the strongest existing demonstration that hippocampal cognitive maps extend to value geometry: value place fields share four diagnostic properties with spatial place cells, so value is map-structured rather than tagged. Confidence set at 0.70, BELOW the Q-020 sibling's 0.78, because MECH-144 is specifically a claim about the VENTRAL compartment and this recording is primate hippocampus without a dorsal/ventral localisation -- the compartment specificity that makes this evidence fit MECH-144 is exactly what the paper does not establish. NOTE ON DIRECTION: this record is 'supports' while the sibling Q-020 record on the same paper is 'weakens'. Both are correct -- the paper weakens Q-020's ARC-007 'hippocampus is value-free' framing precisely BY supporting MECH-144. See the direction-sign note in evidence/planning/literature_claim_tag_audit.md.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Primate hippocampal neurons exhibit 'value place fields' -- spatially tuned responses to positions in an abstract reward-value space defined by the relative value of three choice options. These fields share four properties with spatial place cells: consistency across experiences, multidimensional tuning, directional selectivity, and remapping in novel contexts. They generalize across contexts as experience accumulates.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-144 asserts that valence is intrinsic to hippocampal map geometry rather than externally applied. Knudsen & Wallis supply the constructive half of that claim: the hippocampus does not merely receive a value signal, it builds a map whose axes ARE value. The four-property parallelism with spatial place cells is what makes this a geometry claim rather than a coding claim -- value is represented in the same format as space. For REE this says the residue field R(x,t) can carry a value-structured prior as part of its own representational format, which is the form MECH-144 needs for the MECH-143/MECH-144 dorsal-ventral dissociation to work.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two gaps, and the compartment one is load-bearing for this particular tagging. (1) MECH-144 is stated as a VENTRAL CA1 claim; this is primate hippocampus recorded without a dorsal/ventral assignment, so the paper supports 'hippocampus builds value maps' more directly than it supports 'the ventral compartment does'. (2) The value space here is abstract relative reward magnitude in a choice task, not harm or anxiety geography -- whether value place fields would emerge for aversive residue is untested, and REE's residue field conflates harm, goal, and spatial salience. Both gaps are why confidence is set below the Q-020 sibling's.
mapping.source_context: Primate (macaque) hippocampus; single-unit electrophysiology during abstract value-based decision task; cue values defined by relative reward magnitudes

confidence_components.notes: Source quality unchanged from the Q-020 sibling (0.93) -- same paper, clean primate electrophysiology. Mapping fidelity LOWERED to 0.60 (from 0.68) and transfer risk RAISED to 0.42 (from 0.38): MECH-144 names the ventral compartment specifically and this recording does not localise dorsoventrally, which is a tighter mismatch against MECH-144 than against the compartment-agnostic Q-020. Net overall confidence 0.70 vs the sibling's 0.78.
